title: 1999 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Three non-overlapping regular plane polygons, at least two of which are congruent, all have sides of length \(1.\) The polygons meet at a point \(A\) in such a way that the sum of the three interior angles at \(A\) is \(360^\circ.\) Thus the three polygons form a new polygon with \(A\) as an interior point. What is the largest possible perimeter that this polygon can have?

solutions.text:
Let two congruent \(a\)-gons and one \(b\)-gon meet at \(A.\) Their interior angles satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} &2 \cdot 180\left(1 - \tfrac2a\right) \\ &\quad {}+ 180\left(1 - \tfrac2b\right) = 360, \end{aligned} \] which reduces to \((a - 4)(b - 2) = 8.\)

The solutions \((a, b)\) are \((5, 10), (6, 6), (8, 4),\) and \((12, 3).\) The new polygon’s perimeter is \(2a + b - 6,\) giving \(14, 12, 14,\) and \(21.\) The largest is \(21.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
